Remark.content: Investigation comprised 5 boreholes (BH-1 through BH-5) and 2 out-of-boundary boreholes (BH-1-OUT, BH-2-OUT), totalling approximately 150 m of drilling. In-situ SPT testing performed throughout. Laboratory testing included Atterberg limits, particle size distribution, CBR, and compaction tests. Foundation system comprises 1,075 controlled modulus columns (CMC/rigid inclusions) across 13 load transfer platform zones.

Site geology comprises surficial aeolian sand overlying medium-dense to dense silty sand and sandy silt, with occasional gravel layers. Groundwater not encountered within the investigated depth. Foundation recommendations based on CMC rigid inclusion system with load transfer platform (LTP) of compacted granular fill.

Remark.content: Global Geosolutions Ltd mobilised Rig No. 3 to BH-1 location on the morning of 4 March 2024. Drilling commenced at 06:30 AST and was completed by 17:45 AST.

Borehole BH-1 advanced by rotary wash method to 56.54 m bgl. Potable water with 4–5% bentonite used as drilling fluid. SPT conducted at 2.83 m intervals throughout using an automatic trip hammer (ER = 72%). No caving or fluid loss observed. Borehole fully grouted with cement-bentonite on completion.

Drilling fluid returns observed to be clean and consistent throughout. Cuttings collected at surface at each SPT interval and logged by the attending geotechnical engineer. No refusal encountered above 28.27 m; SPT refusal (N > 50) first recorded at 42.41 m depth.

BoreholeConstructionMethod.holeStability: Stable throughout 56.54 m depth. No caving, no fluid loss, no obstruction. Borehole walls supported by bentonite drilling fluid pressure. Open hole condition maintained without incident from surface to termination depth.

Remark.content: Global Geosolutions Ltd mobilised Rig No. 3 to BH-1 location on the morning of 4 March 2024. Drilling commenced at 06:30 AST and was completed by 17:45 AST.

Borehole BH-1 advanced by rotary wash method to 30.0 m bgl. Potable water with 4–5% bentonite used as drilling fluid. SPT conducted at 1.5 m intervals throughout using an automatic trip hammer (ER = 72%). No caving or fluid loss observed. Borehole fully grouted with cement-bentonite on completion.

Drilling fluid returns observed to be clean and consistent throughout. Cuttings collected at surface at each SPT interval and logged by the attending geotechnical engineer. No refusal encountered above 15.0 m; SPT refusal (N > 50) first recorded at 22.5 m depth.

BoreholeConstructionMethod.holeStability: Stable throughout 30.0 m depth. No caving, no fluid loss, no obstruction. Borehole walls supported by bentonite drilling fluid pressure. Open hole condition maintained without incident from surface to termination depth.

GroutPlant.gml:description: Portable grout plant used for preparation and placement of cement-bentonite grout for borehole backfill completion of BH-1.

BH-1 Backfill Grout Plant

Remark.content: Grouting operations commenced at 16:00 AST following completion of final SPT at 30.0 m and withdrawal of drill string. Cement-bentonite grout tremied from base of borehole to surface.

Portable paddle mixer and diaphragm grout pump used to prepare and place cement-bentonite grout. Grout mix design: OPC 50 kg per 25 litres water with 3% bentonite by dry weight of cement. Specific gravity of grout verified at 1.42 prior to placement.

Grout placed via 25 mm tremie pipe inserted to base of borehole and withdrawn progressively as grout level rose. Total grout volume placed approximately 530 litres. Return of grout observed at surface confirming complete fill of 30.0 m borehole.

Hammer calibration certificate valid until 31 December 2024. Equipment inspected by engineer prior to first SPT of the day. No malfunctions recorded during BH-1 testing.

BH-1 Tremie Grout Injection Assembly

Remark.content: Tremie pipe inserted to base of borehole at 30.0 m prior to commencing grout injection. Pipe withdrawn progressively as grout level rose. Full grout return confirmed at surface by 17:30 AST.

25 mm nominal bore rigid PVC tremie pipe used for grout injection. Pipe sections coupled with threaded joints and lowered to 30.0 m depth prior to pumping. Grout injected under low positive pressure to avoid hydraulic fracture of borehole walls.

Tremie assembly inspected for blockage prior to use. No blockages or flow interruptions recorded during BH-1 grouting operation. Total elapsed injection time approximately 90 minutes for 530 litre volume.

Jazera Site Jet Grouting Monitor — RIFS Works

Remark.content: Bentonite slurry prepared prior to spud-in at 05:45 AST. Mud weight and Marsh funnel viscosity checked hourly throughout drilling operations and adjusted as required to maintain adequate cuttings return and borehole stability.

Mixer inspected and flushed clean prior to mobilisation to site. Motor and impeller in good condition throughout operation. No mechanical faults recorded during BH-1 operations.

Remark.content: Global Geosolutions Ltd mobilised Rig No. 3 to BH-1 location on the morning of 4 March 2024. Drilling commenced at 06:30 AST and was completed by 17:45 AST.

Borehole BH-1 advanced by rotary wash method to 30.0 m bgl. Potable water with 4–5% bentonite used as drilling fluid. SPT conducted at 1.5 m intervals throughout using an automatic trip hammer (ER = 72%). No caving or fluid loss observed. Borehole fully grouted with cement-bentonite on completion.
